web_evidence.title: The Translation of Language-Play in Barbara Kingsolver’s The Poisonwood Bible
web_evidence.note: University of Vaasa structural analysis states that the story is told entirely in first-person narrative by five narrators and describes the mother’s prefaces and daughters’ sections.

web_evidence.title: The Revelatory Narrative Circle in Barbara Kingsolver’s The Poisonwood Bible
web_evidence.note: Journal of Narrative Theory analysis identifies five homodiegetic character-narrators who speak by turns throughout the novel and explicitly contrasts this structure with conventional third-person narration.

person_note: The event quotations repeatedly expose participating Price-family narrators through “I,” “my,” and “we,” while the opened scholarly whole-book sources identify five character-narrators and explicitly describe the novel as entirely first person. The changing speaker does not warrant ALTERNATING because Orleanna, Rachel, Leah, Adah, and Ruth May all narrate in first person. Rhetorical or addressed “you” passages are local direct address or generalization, not sustained second-person narration; bare “she/he” passages do not establish third-person narration. Dialogue and gnomic quotations were treated as non-base, and the final posthumous voice remains a participating first-person voice. No material contrary evidence remains.
